# Agent types (`agent-types/`)

An agent type (a "specialty") is the label an agent is created under. The platform
defines one built-in type, `specialist`, as a typed record in
`lib/specialist-type.ts`; see [specialties.md](specialties.md) for what the record
holds and how extensions register more types. The `agent-types/` directory now holds
only workspace templates:

```
agent-types/
└── specialist/
    └── templates/               # workspace seed files (*.template)
```

## Templates

Seeded into a new agent's workspace by `resolveTemplatesDir()` in `runtime/setup.ts`. A
type's templates live at `<specialties dir>/<specialty>/templates/`; for `specialist`
the record's `templatesDir` (`agent-types/specialist/templates/`, relative to the repo
root) is also tried. Required: `CLAUDE.md.template`, `SOUL.md.template`,
`IDENTITY.md.template`. A type whose directory is missing or lacks one of these falls
back to the built-in `workspace/` directory with a warning; it never fails boot.
`SPECIALTY.md.template` is optional and is layered into the seeded workspace. Any other
file (VOICE, mise, requirements, BOOTSTRAP) falls back per file to the built-in
`workspace/` directory.

An unknown requested type warns and uses the default type's templates; only if the
default type does not resolve either does it fall back to the built-in `workspace/`
directory.

## Resolution at runtime

`admin/src/specialty-types.ts` maps an agent's stored specialty to its type record. The
specialty is read from the required `Agent.specialty` column.

- `SHIPWRIGHT_SPECIALTIES_DIR` overrides the specialties directory (default: the
  shipped `agent-types/`).
- `SHIPWRIGHT_DEFAULT_AGENT_TYPE` overrides the default type name (default
  `specialist`); the admin accepts it as a valid type alongside `specialist`.
- Both defaults come from one shared helper, `lib/default-specialty.ts`, used by the
  admin, `account-agent-create.ts`, the admin UI and the runtime's
  `resolveTemplatesDir()`, so a platform-only boot with neither variable set seeds a
  `specialist` agent from the shipped `agent-types/`.
- `getType()` never throws: every stored specialty, including legacy values, resolves
  to the specialist floor (tools and required env).
- Cron reconciliation uses `tryGetType()` (no fallback): a specialty that is neither
  built in nor supplied crons by an extension logs an error and reconciles nothing.

## The `specialist` type

A generic, non-coding agent: no system crons, no GitHub scope, tools
`Bash`, `WebSearch`, `WebFetch`, `Agent`. Its only required env is
`CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`. Slack, voice and `GH_TOKEN` env are optional and set per
agent. It is meant to be specialized after creation through the admin API.

## Default plugins

Every agent created through the platform (admin form, API, self-serve) is seeded with
`agent-platform@app-vitals-agent`, the platform's own baked-marketplace plugin (the
`slack-say` progress-ping, `agent-admin` and `investigate-cron` skills under
`plugins/agent-platform/skills/`). This is not per-specialty: it comes from
`resolveDefaultPlugins()` in `lib/default-plugins.ts`, which prepends it to any plugins an
extension's `specialtyDefaults()` supplies (deduped), so derived images get it without
per-agent setup. Seeding happens at create time only; existing agents are unchanged.

To enable it on an existing agent, add the plugin row (`POST /agents/:id/plugins` with
`{"name": "agent-platform@app-vitals-agent"}`, or the Plugins tab in the admin UI) and
restart the agent so `installPlugins()` picks it up.

## Adding a type

Register it from an `AdminExtension` (`agentTypes()` and, for defaults,
`specialtyDefaults()`) and ship its templates at
`<specialties dir>/<name>/templates/`. Run `bun run check:boundary`; the directory is
scanned for imports that leave the repo.
